newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Ousted Indonesian MP faces trial for subversion.
newsitem.headline: Ousted Indonesian MP faces trial for subversion.

text.p: Indonesia's Attorney General Singgih said his office had collected enough evidence to try sacked legislator Sri Bintang Pamungkas on subversion charges, the official Antara news agency reported on Tuesday.

Bintang was arrested early this month on charges of subversion, which carry a maximum penalty of death, in relation to Eid al-Fitr greeting cards he sent to various people last month marking the end of the Moslem fasting month of Ramadan.

He had put on the cards the platform of the unrecognised United Democratic Party of Indonesia (PUDI) he founded last year, which included calls for a boycott of general elections in May and the rejection of President Suharto's expected re-election next year.

Bintang already faces a 34-month prison term after the High Court last month upheld a lower court decision finding him guilty of defaming Suharto in a speech to Indonesian students in Germany in April 1995.
He had been free pending a further appeal.

Bintang was sacked in 1995 by the Moslem-oriented United Development Party (PPP), one of the three parties legally entitled to contest the May general elections, for being too oustspoken and as a result lost his seat in the 500-member parliament.
Antara quoted Singgih as saying on Monday his office had "collected enough evidence" to send Bintang for trial despite his refusal to answer questions put to him during questioning.
PUDI secretary-general Julius Usman was also arrested and faces similar subversion charges.
